Yes. The least-annoying clever version is a **single “living” Slack message** that your GitHub Action updates every day, instead of posting a fresh message daily.

Assuming you mean **WeAreDevelopers World Congress Europe in Berlin, July 8-10, 2026**, today is **T-50**. There’s also **North America in San José, September 23-25, 2026**, which is **T-127**.

**Best Pattern**
Post one message, pin it, then update it daily with `chat.update`. Only post a new visible message for milestones like `T-30`, `T-14`, `T-7`, `T-1`, and “we’re live.” Slack supports Block Kit messages, up to 50 blocks per message, and `chat.update` lets you replace the blocks while keeping the same message in place.

Good Slack elements to use:

- **Header block**: `T-50 to WeAreDevelopers`
- **Section fields**: compact metrics like `Days left`, `Next release`, `Booth readiness`, `Last shipped`
- **Context block**: tiny timestamp/source line, e.g. “Updated by GitHub Actions”
- **Buttons**: `Agenda`, `Release notes`, `Booth plan`, `Tickets`
- **Overflow menu**: low-priority actions like `View checklist`, `Mute daily nudges`, `Open GitHub milestone`
- **Workflow button**: trigger an internal Slack workflow like “Submit demo idea” or “Add launch task”
- **Feedback buttons**: “Useful / too much” so the team can tune the cadence
- **Rich text quote**: one tiny daily “why it matters” note

A nice message shape:

```text
T-50 to WeAreDevelopers Berlin

████████░░░░░░░░░░░░ 50 days left

Release pulse
Latest: v0.5.3 shipped yesterday
Next: review command polish
Need today: 1 demo story, 2 customer-proof bullets

[Agenda] [Latest release notes] [Prep checklist] [...]
```

The key is: **daily update, not daily interruption**. I’d only send a thread reply when something changes materially, like a release going out, a CFP/speaker deadline, booth logistics, or a milestone countdown.

Implementation-wise, your GitHub Action can:

1. Run daily on `schedule`.
2. Compute `days_left`.
3. Generate Block Kit JSON.
4. If no stored Slack `message_ts`, call `chat.postMessage`.
5. Otherwise call `chat.update` with the stored `channel` and `ts`.

Docs worth keeping handy: [Slack Block Kit](https://docs.slack.dev/block-kit), [block elements](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/block-elements/), and [`chat.update`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.update).

Use **one message that keeps getting updated**.

Flow:

1. First run: GitHub Action calls `chat.postMessage`:
   `T-50 days left to WeAreDevelopers`
2. Save the Slack `channel` + `message_ts`.
3. Every day: GitHub Action calls [`chat.update`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.update) on that same message:

- Use fewer emoji squares, like 10 or 12.
- Put the count on a separate line.
- Use plain text glyphs instead of emoji, which are visually smaller:

- Use a single status emoji plus text:

